newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Japan credit associations say will merge.
newsitem.headline: Two Japan credit associations say will merge.

text.p: Two Japanese regional credit associations, known as "shinkin" banks, said on Friday that they would merge in February 1998 to cope with changes and liberalisation in Japan"s financial industry.

Chiba Shinkin Bank and Ryoso Shinyokinko, which are both based in Chiba Prefecture, near Tokyo, said in a statement that they would merge on the equal basis to create the largest credit association in the prefecture.
The merged body would be the 33rd largest of Japan"s 411 credit associations, they said.
Chiba Shinkin, currently the second largest of 11 credit associations in the prefecture, had deposits totalling 433.20 billion yen as of the end of December, they said.
Ryoso, the ninth largest in the prefecture, had deposits totalling 140.15 billion yen as of end December, they said.
